newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND TAME ACT IN SUPER 12 CLASH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND TAME ACT IN SUPER 12 CLASH.

text.p: The ACT Brumbies were tamed by a superior Auckland Blues 41-29 in their top-of-the-table Super 12 rugby clash at Auckland's Pukekohe Stadium on Saturday.
The Blues, defending champions, served notice that they were back on form after snatching a fortunate victory against Canterbury a week ago.
ACT's saving grace was a three-try burst in the final six minutes when Auckland were reduced to 14 men after replacement Dylan Mika was sinbinned for a head-high tackle on one of the Brumbies.
Auckland drew first blood in the sixth minute, with inside centre Lee Stensness racing away for a try and fullback Adrian Cashmore adding the extras, giving the Blues a 7-0 lead.
David Knox cut the Blues lead with a penalty goal after ACT scrum-half George Gregan was taken in a high tackle by Michael Jones.
Shortly into the second half Blues debutant lock Leo Lafaiali'i set the scene for a strong performance in the remainder of the game with the Blues' third try.
Near the end of the game, ACT scored three tries in a rush through replacement Rod Kafer, fullback Larkham and another replacement Ipolito Fenukitau to narrow the score to 41-29.
"Can we just talk about the last five minutes?" said a naturally disappointed ACT coach Rod MacQueen.
Auckland Blues coach Graham Henry described the performance as his team's best effort so far this year.
The Brumbies now take on the Otago Highlanders in Invercargill on Thursday while the Blues face the Gauteng Lions.
